info.title: Divinci Public/Customer API
info.description: Public API for managing whitelabels, RAG knowledge bases, releases, fine-tuning, transcripts, and more. This spec is auto-generated from the Express route definitions in workspace/servers/public-api/src/api/v1 — every path and method is guaranteed to match the shipped server.

tags.name: chat
tags.description:
Chat completions and thread management. `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` is an OpenAI-style completion endpoint that lets you call your Divinci release like a model — same request shape OpenAI clients already speak. Use this for drop-in compatibility with existing tooling; prefer the dedicated SDKs (`@divinci-ai/server`, `@divinci-ai/client`) when you want streaming, RAG context, and Divinci-specific features.

`curl -X POST -H "x-api-key: $KEY" https://api.divinci.ai/api/v1/chat/completions -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hi"}]}'`

tags.name: connectors
tags.description:
Third-party provider connections (Neo4j, search graphs, and other external integrations). Use these endpoints to list available providers, inspect a connection's status, kick off the provider's OAuth/auth flow, and disconnect a previously-linked account. Connection credentials are stored as BYOK records — see the `byok` resource for direct credential CRUD. Requires `connector:read` for GET and `connector:write` for changes.

`curl -H "x-api-key: $KEY" https://api.divinci.ai/api/v1/connectors`

tags.name: copilot
tags.description:
Divinci Copilot orchestration. Drives the multi-step agent that produces release recommendations, content drafts, and other long-running suggestions. `GET /api/v1/copilot/health` is a public liveness check; the orchestration `POST /api/v1/copilot` requires an API key. Most customer integrations use the dashboard UI over this — the endpoints are exposed for advanced automation and CI hooks.

`curl https://api.divinci.ai/api/v1/copilot/health`

tags.name: divinci-agent
tags.description:
Divinci Agent transcript bridge — reads and syncs transcripts produced by the on-platform agent into your own systems. `GET /api/v1/divinci-agent/health` is a liveness check. `GET /api/v1/divinci-agent/transcript` lists agent transcripts; `POST .../sync` triggers a re-sync of a specific transcript's messages from the upstream agent store; `.../messages` returns the synced message list. Use this when you need agent-generated transcripts in a downstream warehouse or webhook destination.

`curl -H "x-api-key: $KEY" https://api.divinci.ai/api/v1/divinci-agent/transcript/{transcriptId}/messages`

tags.name: export
tags.description:
Bulk data export for a workspace. `POST /api/v1/export` enqueues an asynchronous export of the workspace's records (transcripts, RAG metadata, configuration) and returns a job handle you can poll for the download URL. Use this for compliance, migration, or feeding analytics warehouses. Heavy operation — rate-limited per workspace.

`curl -X POST -H "x-api-key: $KEY" https://api.divinci.ai/api/v1/export -d '{"scope":"transcripts"}'`

tags.name: html-pages
tags.description:
URL-indexed HTML pages — Divinci's surface for scraping, storing, and querying snapshots of web pages so they can be referenced in RAG and agent flows. `POST /api/v1/html-pages` ingests a URL; `GET /api/v1/html-pages` lists indexed pages with pagination; `/count`, `/by-url`, and `/hosts`-rooted endpoints provide aggregations for dashboards. Each host also keeps a versioned history (`/hosts/history`, `/hosts/{urlHost}/history`) and individual pages are addressable by `pageId`.

`curl -H "x-api-key: $KEY" https://api.divinci.ai/api/v1/html-pages?limit=20`

tags.name: mcp-config
tags.description:
MCP server configuration per whitelabel. `GET /api/v1/mcp-config/{whitelabelId}` returns the MCP capabilities, tool exposure, and pricing-tier policy for a whitelabeled deployment. Use this to provision MCP-aware AI assistants (Claude Desktop, Cursor) against a customer-specific Divinci instance. Whitelabel-gated — most non-whitelabel deployments will not need it.

`curl -H "x-api-key: $KEY" https://api.divinci.ai/api/v1/mcp-config/{whitelabelId}`

tags.name: notifications
tags.description:
In-app notification center. `GET /api/v1/notifications` lists notifications for the authenticated user; `GET /api/v1/notifications/counts` returns unread totals for a badge UI; `POST /api/v1/notifications/{notificationId}/read` marks one as read. Use these when embedding the Divinci notification bell in your own dashboard.

`curl -H "x-api-key: $KEY" https://api.divinci.ai/api/v1/notifications/counts`

tags.name: tts
tags.description:
Text-to-speech generation and per-workspace TTS settings. `POST /api/v1/tts/generate` synthesizes audio from a text payload using the workspace's default voice; `GET/PUT /api/v1/tts/settings` reads/writes voice, speed, and provider preferences. Pair with `audio-transcripts` for a full voice-in / voice-out pipeline.

`curl -X POST -H "x-api-key: $KEY" https://api.divinci.ai/api/v1/tts/generate -d '{"text":"Hello"}'`

tags.name: voiceprints
tags.description:
Voice biometrics — register, list, and verify voiceprints used for caller / speaker authentication on voice integrations. `GET /api/v1/voiceprints` lists the current workspace's enrollments. Treat voiceprint registration as PII; restrict the API key permission scope accordingly.

`curl -H "x-api-key: $KEY" https://api.divinci.ai/api/v1/voiceprints`

get.summary: GET /api/v1/rag/files/:fileId/vectorize-status — Definitive readiness check. Cloudflare Vectorize is eventually consistent (~10–60s); this endpoint directly verifies the file's chunks are queryable instead of relying on the file's status field, which can flip to "completed" before vectors are searchable.
GET /api/v1/rag/files/:fileId/chunks — List paginated chunks for a file Query params: offset (default 0), limit (default 25, max 100)

POST /api/v1/chat/completions OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint. Sends a message and returns the AI response synchronously. Body: { messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hello" }],  // Required — last message is sent transcriptId?: string,  // Optional — reuse existing transcript for context stream?: boolean,       // Reserved for future streaming support (currently ignored) } Response: { id: string, object: "chat.completion", choices: [{ index: 0, message: { role: "assistant", content: "..." }, finish_reason: "stop" }], usage: { prompt_tokens: 0, completion_tokens: 0, total_tokens: 0 }, }
